function_v0.doc:
Replace the Factory Wasm. Auth: admin (checked BEFORE the swap).

Added alongside `Registry::upgrade` (2026-08-01): the Factory permanently
holds every owner\xe2\x86\x92strategy mapping and anchors each strategy's
deterministic address, so a redeploy loses the index AND breaks
`predict_address` continuity \xe2\x80\x94 it must be patchable in place.
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc: The owner's deployed slot numbers (sparse, e.g. {0, 5, 42}) in deploy order.\nLets the indexer/api recover the true `slot` for each strategy (paired with\n`strategy_at`) and compute the next free slot \xe2\x80\x94 never assume dense 0..count.
function_v0.name: owner_slots

function_v0.doc: The strategy at `(owner, index)`, or `None` if that slot is free.
function_v0.name: strategy_at

function_v0.doc: All of the owner's deployed strategies (empty for a not-yet-deployed owner).\nIterates the sparse `OwnerSlots` \xe2\x80\x94 never `0..count`.
function_v0.name: strategy_of

function_v0.doc: Accept a proposed admin rotation, step 2 of 2. Auth: the NOMINEE.
function_v0.name: accept_admin

function_v0.doc:
Rotate the admin, step 1 of 2. Auth: current admin. Nothing changes until
the nominee calls `accept_admin`.

Two-step for the same reason as the Registry, and it matters more here:
the Factory admin owns `set_strategy_wasm`, which decides the CODE every
future strategy deploys with. Losing it means the template can never be
updated again \xe2\x80\x94 and `require_admin` gates `upgrade` too, so there is no
path back. The nominee signing step 2 proves the key can sign before it
takes effect.
function_v0.name: transfer_admin

function_v0.doc: Deploy the owner's Strategy at `index` and `fund` a deposit intent in one\nsigned tx \xe2\x80\x94 the first-deposit path for a selection too large to `invest`\natomically. Auth: owner (whole tree).
function_v0.name: deploy_and_fund

function_v0.doc:
Deploy the owner's Strategy at slot `index`, at its deterministic address.
Auth: owner. One per `(owner, index)` (`AlreadyDeployed` otherwise);
refuses past `OWNER_SLOT_CAP` slots per owner (`TooManyStrategies`).

`auto_rebalance` is the strategy's IMMUTABLE lifetime choice (doc 13): a
strategy is born keeper-managed or manual, and pays `fee_bps + delta` or
`fee_bps` accordingly, until it is closed. There is no setter afterwards.
function_v0.name: deploy_strategy

function_v0.doc: Deterministic Strategy address for `(owner, index)` (computable pre-deploy).
function_v0.name: predict_address

function_v0.doc: Deploy the owner's Strategy at `index` and run the first `invest` in one\nsigned tx (the default first-investment path). Auth: owner (whole tree).
function_v0.name: deploy_and_invest

function_v0.doc: Set the template Wasm hash used by FUTURE deploys. Auth: admin.
function_v0.name: set_strategy_wasm

function_v0.doc: How many slots the owner has deployed (a count, not a max index).
function_v0.name: strategy_count_of

function_v0.doc:
Upgrade many Strategies in ONE admin-signed envelope. Auth: admin.

**Why this exists.** Every Strategy is constructed with the Factory's admin
as its own admin (see `deploy_strategy`), and `Strategy::upgrade` is gated
on that address. Soroban permits one `InvokeHostFunction` per transaction,
so rolling a new template across the fleet was one full 2-of-3 ceremony
PER INSTANCE \xe2\x80\x94 and the instance count only grows. The admin's single root
authorization covers the sub-invocations, collapsing a batch into one
envelope. Same shape `deploy_and_invest` already uses to reach into a
freshly deployed Strategy under one owner-signed tree.

The Factory does NOT need to be each Strategy's admin: the auth that
satisfies `Strategy::upgrade` is the admin's, carried down the tree from
this call. The Factory only supplies the invocation.

Addresses are taken as an argument rather than read from the Factory's own
index on purpose \xe2\x80\x94 the caller decides the batch, so a partially-completed
roll is resumed by passing the remainde
function_v0.name: upgrade_strategies

udt_struct_v0.doc: Declaration only \xe2\x80\x94 nothing decodes into it any more (see\n`fetch_total_managed_funds`). Retained because it is in the deployed type spec,\nand dropping it would make the upgrade non-additive (preflight \xc2\xa74b).
udt_struct_v0.name: CurrentAssetInvestmentAllocation

udt_struct_v0.doc: A funded-but-unfilled deposit. At most ONE per Strategy at a time.
udt_struct_v0.name: Intent

fields.doc: The asset every leg is denominated in (== each leg vault's underlying).
fields.name: asset

fields.doc: Ledger timestamp after which only the OWNER may fill.
fields.name: deadline

fields.doc: Monotonic id \xe2\x80\x94 the at-most-once guard and the event-correlation key.
fields.name: id

fields.doc: UNFILLED legs. A filled leg is REMOVED; when empty the Intent is deleted.\nLegs are addressed by `vault`, so vaults are unique within one intent.
fields.name: legs

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A single Soroswap swap leg. Full shape frozen at T1; the swap *logic* is
activated by config: the gen-4 Registry router is SET (`CAG5LRYQ\xe2\x80\xa6`, verified
2026-09-22), so a leg carrying this executes. It reverts only while a router is
unset, which is no longer the deployed state.
udt_struct_v0.name: SwapLeg

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Per-vault position + fee-engine accounting.

There is no `banked_fee`: `auto_rebalance` is an immutable create-time choice,
so a strategy's fee rate never changes during its life. Rate-period banking
existed only to keep a rate CHANGE non-retroactive; with no change possible it
is provably always zero, and the whole mechanism is gone (doc 13).
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.doc: Basis / high-water mark: `profit = max(0, value - deposit_amount)`.
fields.name: deposit_amount

fields.doc: Snapshot of `VaultInfo.fee_bps` at the first deposit into this vault.
fields.name: fee_bps

udt_union_v0.doc: Underlying-protocol tag stored alongside each whitelisted vault; the Strategy\ndispatches the right adapter by matching on this (no `_` arm \xe2\x80\x94 adding a\nprotocol is an exhaustive-match break on purpose). T2 adds `DeFindex`; T3 +1.
udt_union_v0.name: Protocol

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One leg of a funded deposit intent: an EXACT amount of the intent asset
destined for one whitelisted vault.

Amounts are ABSOLUTE, computed at `fund` time from the MEASURED post-swap
balance \xe2\x80\x94 never weights re-derived at fill time against a balance that has
since moved.
udt_struct_v0.name: IntentLeg

udt_union_v0.doc:
An optional swap. Semantically `Option<SwapLeg>`, but expressed as a dedicated
`#[contracttype]` enum: soroban-sdk 26 cannot derive the (testutils) XDR
conversions for an `Option<CustomStruct>` *struct field*, because the
`Option<T> -> ScVal` blanket requires `T: Into<ScVal>` (infallible) while a
`#[contracttype]` struct is only `TryFrom<_> for ScVal` (fallible). An enum
goes through the Val path and has no such bound.

Used by `fund`, which converts the WHOLE deposit in one hop or not at all.
udt_union_v0.name: MaybeSwap

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One Reflector price sample. `price` is scaled by the oracle's own `decimals()`
(14 on mainnet) and denominated in the oracle's `base()` asset \xe2\x80\x94 which for the
Stellar-asset oracle IS our USDC SAC, so a Backyard swap bound needs ONE feed
read, not a two-feed USD derivation.
udt_struct_v0.name: PriceData

fields.doc: Unix seconds of the sample. Compared against `max_price_age` \xe2\x80\x94 a stale feed\nmust REVERT, never fall through to an unbounded swap.
fields.name: timestamp

udt_struct_v0.doc: Registry record for one whitelisted vault.
udt_struct_v0.name: VaultInfo

fields.doc: `false` delists the vault for **new** deposits only; never blocks exits.
fields.name: active

fields.doc: Base performance fee for this vault (engine `VaultState.feeBps`).\n`0` = no fee (the T1 default until a % is configured).
fields.name: fee_bps

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One leg of an `invest` allocation.

There is deliberately NO per-leg swap here. `invest` performs ONE swap per
distinct vault underlying (see `strategy/src/invest.rs`), because the
per-transaction budget is bound by the number of router calls, not by the
number of legs. The swap legs travel alongside as a
`Map<underlying, SwapLeg>`.
udt_struct_v0.name: Allocation

udt_struct_v0.doc: Post-state for one deposit leg, carried in the `Deposited` event so the\nindexer mirrors fee state with no live read.
udt_struct_v0.name: DepositLeg

udt_union_v0.doc: Reflector / SEP-40 asset discriminant. `Stellar(Address)` for a Soroban token,\n`Other(Symbol)` for an off-chain ticker. Backyard only ever prices Stellar\nassets, but the enum must match the oracle's ABI exactly or the call traps.
udt_union_v0.name: OracleAsset

udt_union_v0.doc:
How a withdrawal returns funds. Both variants are handled live by
`withdraw.rs::deliver`: `Raw` returns the redeemed underlying as-is, and
`Normalize` swaps each redeemed underlying into `asset` via the router. A
same-asset `Normalize` succeeds without a swap; a real cross-asset swap
reverts `AdapterError` while the Router is unset (dormant-by-config, not
rejected by shape) and activates by config \xe2\x80\x94 the signature never changes.
(soroban-sdk `#[contracttype]` enums don't allow named-field variants, so the
payload is a one-field wrapper struct.)
udt_union_v0.name: WithdrawOut

udt_struct_v0.doc: Per-vault weight in a `fund` plan. A dedicated type rather than reusing\n[`Allocation`], whose per-leg `swap` field is meaningless here: `fund`\nperforms exactly ONE swap for the whole deposit.
udt_struct_v0.name: IntentWeight

udt_struct_v0.doc: Normalize-out payload: swap each redeemed underlying into `asset` before\nreturning it to the owner (T2). `swaps` maps source-underlying \xe2\x86\x92 its leg.
udt_struct_v0.name: NormalizeOut

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Registry oracle configuration for the keeper-path swap floor.

Fail-closed by absence: while this is unset the keeper cannot swap at all,
which is the same stance the (empty) per-hop allowlist takes.
udt_struct_v0.name: OracleConfig

fields.doc:
The oracle's OWN base asset \xe2\x80\x94 what its prices are denominated in
(`base()`; our USDC SAC on mainnet).

Pinned explicitly rather than inferred. The base has no feed of its own \xe2\x80\x94
it is 1:1 by definition \xe2\x80\x94 and an earlier draft inferred "no feed \xe2\x87\x92 must be
the base" from the swap allowlist. That was wrong and dangerous: by the
time the floor runs, every hop has ALREADY passed the allowlist, so the
inference was always true and any allowlisted asset the oracle could not
price would have been valued 1:1 against the base. Naming it removes the
guess.
fields.name: base

fields.doc: Oracle `decimals()` \xe2\x80\x94 pinned at config time so the Strategy does not spend\na second cross-contract call per swap discovering it.
fields.name: decimals

fields.doc: Max age of a price sample, in seconds. Reflector's `resolution()` is 300 s\non mainnet, so this should be a small multiple of it.
fields.name: max_price_age

fields.doc: How far below the oracle-implied output a keeper swap may land.
fields.name: max_slippage_bps

event_v0.doc:
The owner funded a deposit intent: assets pulled, ONE swap performed, proceeds
left idle, per-vault legs recorded. Nothing is deposited yet.

Owner-topic'd like [`Deposited`], so the indexer must key the strategy off the
EMITTING contract id (cross-checked against Factory `StrategyDeployed`), never
off the `strategy` field in the body \xe2\x80\x94 a foreign contract can emit a look-alike.
event_v0.name: Funded

params.doc: What the legs are denominated in (== each leg vault's underlying).
params.name: target

params.doc: MEASURED post-swap amount backing the legs (\xce\xa3 legs.amount == received).
params.name: received

event_v0.doc:
Admin emergency (`rescue`) \xe2\x80\x94 funds go ONLY to Owner; no fee.

`is_full` mirrors `Withdrawn.is_full` and exists for the same reason: an
adapter whose exit is bounded by something other than our own balance (Gami
clamps to the vault's idle cash) can recover only a slice, and `rescue` then
KEEPS the Position. Removing the mirror row on every `Rescued` would hide a
position that still holds shares. Absent on events predating this field, where
a rescue was always a full close \xe2\x80\x94 treat a missing value as `true`.
event_v0.name: Rescued

event_v0.doc: `Some` = upsert, `None` = removed.
event_v0.name: VaultSet

params.doc: (vault, amount_in, received, deposit_amount_after) \xe2\x80\x94 post-state per leg.
params.name: legs

event_v0.doc: `withdraw_all`'s `extra_idle` drain \xe2\x80\x94 one event per idle asset returned RAW\nto the owner (no engine call, no fee).
event_v0.name: IdleSwept

event_v0.doc: Admin set/rotated the global keeper (`set_keeper`).
event_v0.name: KeeperSet

event_v0.doc: Soroswap router updated (used from T2).
event_v0.name: RouterSet

params.doc:
`burned == total` \xe2\x80\x94 every share gone, the Position was CLOSED on-chain.
The indexer must key row deletion off THIS, not off `deposit_amount_after
== 0`: a partial redeem can zero the basis while shares remain (see
`withdraw.rs::settle_one`), and closing the row there would hide a live
position from the UI.
params.name: is_full

event_v0.doc: Admin rotation, step 2: the nominee accepted (`accept_admin`).
event_v0.name: AdminChanged

params.doc: The contract whose admin rotated \xe2\x80\x94 Strategy, Registry or Factory.
params.name: contract

event_v0.doc: Protocol-wide fee config updated (`set_fee_config`).
event_v0.name: FeeConfigSet

event_v0.doc: One intent leg was deposited into its vault. Carries the post-state so the\nindexer mirrors the basis with no live read.
event_v0.name: IntentFilled

params.doc: Legs still unfilled AFTER this one. `0` \xe2\x87\x92 the intent is complete and gone.
params.name: remaining_legs

params.doc: Who paid for this transaction. Fills are permissionless, so this is not\nnecessarily the owner or the Backyard filler.
params.name: filled_by

event_v0.doc: Admin opted an asset in/out of the keeper-path `rebalance_swap` allowlist\n(`set_swap_asset`). The allowlist ships EMPTY \xe2\x80\x94 a keeper cannot swap until an\nadmin lists the output asset here.
event_v0.name: SwapAssetSet

event_v0.doc: Hybrid no-op receipt: target breached, no feasible move. `reason` is a\nCLOSED SET (authoritative): `APY_BREACH | WEIGHT_DRIFT | RISK_BREACH`.
event_v0.name: RebalanceNoOp

event_v0.doc: Owner dropped the bookkeeping row for a vault holding ZERO shares\n(`close_position`). No funds move; the forfeited fields are carried so the\nindexer can close its mirror row and explain the basis that went with it.
event_v0.name: PositionClosed

event_v0.doc: The owner dropped a pending intent. The funds stay as the Strategy's idle\nbalance \xe2\x80\x94 recoverable via `withdraw_all`'s `extra_idle` or `rebalance_deposit`.
event_v0.name: IntentCancelled

event_v0.doc: Admin set/updated the keeper-swap oracle floor (`set_oracle_config`).
event_v0.name: OracleConfigSet

event_v0.doc: `withdraw_all` terminal receipt (T1). `exited` = vaults fully redeemed,\n`skipped` = vaults whose `redeem` reverted (frozen protocol). A non-empty\n`skipped` signals a PARTIAL exit so the indexer marks those positions stuck.
event_v0.name: WithdrawAllDone

params.doc: CLOSED \xe2\x80\x94 `is_full`, the Position row is gone.
params.name: exited

params.doc:
Money moved and a fee settled, but the Position SURVIVES. An adapter whose
exit is bounded by something other than our own balance (Gami clamps to the
vault's idle cash) can recover a slice and leave the rest. Absent on events
from wasm predating this field, where no adapter could produce the state \xe2\x80\x94
treat a missing value as an empty list.
params.name: partial

params.doc: Nothing happened: no burn, no fee, still invested.
params.name: skipped

event_v0.doc:
Registry/Factory Wasm replaced (`upgrade`). The Strategy has its own
[`Upgraded`] event (kept as-is \xe2\x80\x94 its `strategy` topic is ABI-frozen and the
indexer already keys on it); this one covers the two config contracts, where
the emitting contract IS the topic.
event_v0.name: ContractUpgraded

event_v0.doc: Admin global kill-switch (`set_keeper_enabled`).
event_v0.name: KeeperEnabledSet

params.doc: The IMMUTABLE create-time auto-rebalance choice. Carried here so the\nindexer learns it at ingest \xe2\x80\x94 there is no toggle event any more.
params.name: auto_rebalance

params.doc: `burned == total` \xe2\x80\x94 the source Position was CLOSED. See `Withdrawn.is_full`.
params.name: is_full

event_v0.doc:
Admin upgraded a batch of Strategies through `Factory::upgrade_strategies`.

`count` rather than the address list: the list is already in the transaction's
own invocation tree, and an event large enough to hold a fleet is an event the
indexer pays for on every read. The receipt answers "a roll happened, this big,
to this hash" \xe2\x80\x94 reconciling WHICH instances is a per-instance executable-hash
read, which is the only trustworthy check anyway.
event_v0.name: StrategiesUpgraded

event_v0.doc:
Admin CLEARED the keeper-swap oracle floor (`clear_oracle_config`).

Its own event, not an `OracleConfigSet` with empty fields: this is the widest
blast radius of any admin action on the Registry \xe2\x80\x94 every keeper swap across the
whole fleet reverts `OracleUnset` afterwards \xe2\x80\x94 and an indexer or alert must be
able to match on it without first decoding five fields to discover they are
absent. Carries the config that was in force, so the receipt says what was lost.
event_v0.name: OracleConfigCleared

event_v0.doc: Strategy admin rotation, step 1: current admin nominates a successor\n(`transfer_admin`). Not yet in force \xe2\x80\x94 the nominee must `accept_admin`.
event_v0.name: AdminTransferProposed

params.doc: The contract whose admin is being rotated \xe2\x80\x94 Strategy, Registry or Factory.\nNamed `contract`, not `strategy`: all three emit this now that the config\ncontracts also rotate in two steps.
params.name: contract
